title: Two Roads, One Whistle
summary: Two sisters split at a fork with one rule: whistle every hour so the dead follow the whistler. Then one whistle goes quiet.

beats.text: Our rule: whistle twice every hour. The dead follow the whistler. The other sister walks free.
My sister Joan and I split at the fork. One road each.
Noon. I whistled twice. Branches snapped. The whole wood began to lean my way.
Joan's whistle drifted from the east. Her road was quiet. Mine was filling up.
I hid while thirty shuffled past, chasing my own whistle.
Dusk. Her whistle stopped. One hour. Two hours. Nothing but wind.
If I stopped, the dead would turn toward her road. So I could never stop.
I whistled all night. My lips went numb.
Dawn. The bridge. A hundred stood below it, every face turned to my road.
Far ahead, Joan crossed in silence, unseen. She mouthed two words: thank you.
